content:
Where am I today I am writing a travel blog after 8 years. Back in 2017 when I started my job and started earning, I thought I would do 2 trips (1 international, and 1 within India) and write about it. In 2017-2018, I did start strong writing some of my travel experiences on Quora. It was also very deeply appreciated by my family and my colleagues. But as it happened, I gave in to my own laziness, procrastination and entirely stopped writing. Ever since then, after numerous trips, it’s now 2026 and I finally feel the urge to write again once in a while.
This trip was done with family and was mostly a dream wish of Lily Aunty (LA). Bhaskar Uncle (BU) decided to plan this surprise for her just before her 50th birthday (September 1, 2026). Swathi (SM) did all the planning, optimizing every bit of the travel, deciding places to visit, places to eat, the perfect timing to catch sunsets. And I had the least contribution, just made sure I was present and giving good company. Yes, I did some of the booking while optimizing the credit card points. And yes, this trip was just after a sweet promotion, so the previous months had been hectic and I did need a shut-off period from work.
That said, as with most of my trips I had done zero research on the places and the order in which we were travelling. This became embarrassing to a point that I could not tell my colleagues the names of places I was visiting during lunch conversations.
About the trip Day 1 — Madurai SM and I met LA & BU at the Bengaluru Airport. SM was angry at me forgetting to carry my credit card and the chance of us not being allowed into the airport lounge where LA and BU had been waiting over a 4-hour layover. But thanks to all the digital enhancements, I was able to scan a QR and enter. A flight later, we were in Madurai where we were supposed to spend the night and prepare for an early morning darshan of Meenakshi temple. We got up by 6am, clicked a few pictures and were ready to visit the temple. This was the first time I was seeing a gopuram in person, beyond what I had only seen and read in history books (6th grade Indian history). The colors on the gopuram were unique, unlike anything I had ever seen. There were long queues, but it struck me that people were patient, not shouting unlike many other temple towns. We did get help from someone near the queue who helped with expediting the queue and we could do a quick darshan. On our way out, BU was rushing as usual and LA asked us all to sit near the ‘Potramarai Kulam’, or the sacred lotus tank. SM and I again gasped looking at the gopuram, recalled our history classes and then went out.
We then got ready and prepared to head for our next stop - Rameswaram. Just as we were exiting Madurai, SM had researched the perfect place to have ‘Jigarthanda’. I had heard about it from my colleagues as well. And I have to say it’s one of the best things I have had that is so unique to Madurai and not available anywhere else.
Day 2 — Rameswaram Drive to Rameswaram was a 4 hour drive. The Jigarthanda drink made sure we had no appetite for any lunch on the way. We had plans to see Dhanushkodi on the way, which has so much historical significance - The ghost town, Ram Setu and also the last motorable point in India. The first thing that struck us was the distinct color gradients of water when we stood on ‘Pamban’ bridge. Then we headed for the southernmost point. At this point it was about 4pm and we were starting to feel hungry with no sights of any food joints. Here we saw some shacks by the beach and local women cooking fresh-caught fish. SM and I got down to take a look and were hesitant just when BU joined us and said we can try 1 piece. We 3 sat down and the lady got us 1 piece of fried fish. We immediately finished it off and before we knew, we were done with 6 pieces of fish and a plate of prawns. It’s among the best traditional fish I have had and this is something I have always expected from any coastal town but seldom find.
We then checked into our hotel and did the first round of darshan at Rameswaram in the evening. After that we were supposed to come again at 4am and do the Spatika Lingam / Mani Darshan. I’d say it was hard to get up at 3am but I guess that’s the whole point of a Teerth Yatra. It’s supposed to be difficult in the sense that you’d have to turn away from your usual schedules. After the Mani Darshan, we took a plunge in the sea. BU and I entered first, water was not very cold and it felt divine in the sense that Lord Ram is believed to have done something similar after coming back from Lanka. We then did the 22 Kund Snan which is believed to purify the soul and cleanse our sins. LA jokingly said we can commit new sins now that old sins are cleaned.
Rameswaram temple was a bit different in the sense that though it is one of the 4 Dhams, it was not as crowded as others. Maybe I am just traumatized at how difficult it has become to visit Puri (one of the other Dhams) even as a localite. Also, I am still very curious about how this temple serves Lord Shiva whereas all the other Dhams serve Lord Vishnu. I still have some digging left for mythological facts about this. After this we returned to the hotel, had a good breakfast and left for Kanyakumari.
Day 3 — Kanyakumari Drive to Kanyakumari was supposed to be a long one - 6.5 hours from Rameswaram. It was also tiring in the sense we were all up by 3am and already had a long day. BU was mostly sleeping in the car through this journey. The rest of us were dozing and waking up. It was also a very hot day, but overall good roads which made the journey less tiring. We reached Kanyakumari about 4pm and first did a darshan of Kanyakumari Bhagavathi Amman Temple which is a Shakti Peeth. Then we headed straight to the sunset point of ‘Vivekananda Rock Memorial’. This place was pretty scenic and again was a popular place which we always read in our history books. Sunset at this point was truly beautiful. We then headed to our hotel, had a good dinner, coffee and then a quick late night walk where BU and I chatted about whether a hotel in a temple town could be a good business. Both of us agreed it might be a good future option to do something in Puri.
We had a sumptuous buffet breakfast and then set out for our final destination - Trivandrum.
Day 4 — Trivandrum Drive to Trivandrum was scenic as we were now entering Kerala. We were supposed to take a halt at Kovalam - a small beach town and have some seafood. BU had asked me for a promotion party and I had promised him we would have prawns and lobster here. SM has never been to Goa so I had told her that the seafood here at Kovalam might be similar. Kovalam beach side was a retreat in the sense it was small cafes, good coffee, very little crowd and good shacks serving seafood. Maybe it was just the timing of our visit. We quickly scanned through the pre-decided pinned restaurants but realized most of them were closed. SM and I quickly scanned a local shack where the food looked delicious with live fish and lobster for display. We then quickly called up BU and LA and the 4 of us had a gala time eating and raving about the seafood. Hands down, it’s the best seafood I have had outside our homes in Odisha and the best value for money.
We were just walking by the beach and BU asked if I was interested in coffee. And for the nth time on this trip we both had good coffee. I realized it’s such a delightful view to look at the sea and sip coffee and slow down the rush of life. Given a chance, I’d like to come here and enjoy a week off—maybe slow living. We then quickly bid adieu to Kovalam and set out for a short stop at the ‘Aazhimala Shiva Temple’ that had a grand Lord Shiva statue. SM was particularly impressed by the minute details of the sculpture, particularly the way Ganga was emerging from Shiva’s hair. After this we headed out into the city of Trivandrum and checked into our hotel for the night.
The final morning, we prepared to visit the ‘Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple’. This was the only temple on our trip which was strict about what people wore. Even the security guards inside the temple were dressed in the same attire. SM and I had bought my dhoti from Bengaluru. This darshan was magically quick (~30 minutes). But I somehow wish we took more time to look inside. We then took our flights out from Trivandrum. I purchased some books from the Airport. SM, BU and LA left for Bhubaneswar and I went back to Bengaluru.
Post the trip I had been thinking of writing this experience for a month now. And I could have very easily let this slip as yet another procrastinated effort. But this time I am just more determined. And not bad that I have been able to finish writing this just a month from the trip. All these places were clean and left a calming impact on my mind, especially compared to the hustle of Bengaluru.

I am writing a travel blog after 8 years. Back in 2017 when I started my job and started earning, I thought I would do 2 trips (1 international, and 1 within India) and write about it. content:
Referrals are a way for an existing employee to endorse someone who wishes work at Amazon. An endorsement does not guarantee an interview, however with any large sized companies, referrals are a really nice way to increase the chances that your resume at the least gets screened by a recruiter. Most people are aware of this benefit of referral. With platforms like Quora/LinkedIn, it has also become very easy for someone to discover present employees at any of the firms, however I’d like to point out a few flaws with a blind approach for a referral.
The referral process has some benefits for me as well as the candidate who I am referring. For me if the candidate I referred clears the interviews and decides to join Amazon, I get some bonus money. I am not too sure about the exact amount and it anyway keeps changing. For me the motivation is not really earning the additional X dollars from the referral bonus. The intent is to help others achieve their dreams. Referrals are also supposed to help Amazon filter candidates and reach out to those selected folks who have been endorsed by employees already working there. Hence, as an employee I have certain responsibilities to filter the referral requests and make an informed choice about who I want to refer.
I get about 5 new requests each day on LinkedIn/Quora where students and professionals ask me to look at their resume and help them with referrals. As much as I would like to help each of you, my time is limited. Hence more often than not, I might not be able to even reply to your messages on time. In this post I would like to jot down how I would want people to approach someone for referrals by giving some examples of what one should and shouldn’t do while making an approach.
I find above request to be pretty effective because of the below reasons.
Straight way makes the point that there is interest to obtain a referral. A lot of times I get messages like “Hi Sir”, “Hi Sir, How are you?”. One may have a lot of achievements. Listing down the top three is a really nice way to convey your point about why you deem yourself as suitable for a referral. Additionally you could back your proficiency in competitive coding by providing ratings on Codeforces/Codechef. If you not into competitive programming, you could talk about if you are prepared for the role by citing “Solved X problems on InterviewBit, Y problems on LeetCode”. Now let’s see some type of requests that one should absolutely avoid.
Unfortunately, majority of the requests that I get is of this sort. Let’s see the reasons why this form of request is not effective.
“Very good in data structures and algorithm” - The statement has no credibility. There is an attached resume but I wouldn’t really download this. At max I will visit your LinkedIn profile (if I can access). The resume will be used once I have made my mind to refer you. My apologies to the many people who I have not been able to reply. Hope this post provides some perspective on how to effectively approach someone for a referral. The ideal approach request should have the below information,
A two liner introduction about yourself. Your top-3 achievements. A list of 3–4 Job Ids that you consider yourself suitable for. All leading companies have a careers website where you can surf suitable jobs and find the Job Id. Here is Amazon’s job portal. Your resume. I will only be using this to put in the referral. For most instances, I trust your word when you describe your achievements. Originally published on Quora.

content:
Edit: I recalled the difficulty I had to hit the right links for my interests when I passed first year. So I have decided to include some links and references in the answer.
This answer is for the students who come to college without much exposure on the various fields in CSE.
In the first year, during college participate in as many club events (try out Web Dev, App Dev, Competitive Coding, Paper Presentation). After you have seen a bit of everything, it will be easier to realize your strengths and weaknesses. It is completely all right if you have a lot of weaknesses as long as you have a single strength. During the holidays you can enroll yourself in a MOOC course to see if you are really interested in the topic that you feel you are good at. Below are some links to check for the more powerful MOOCs out there.
Computer Science courses on MOOC List Which is the best MOOC for learning CS? If you are reading this, then thumbs up, you are already part of a great Community, Quora. Read on topics here. A simple search on the web will lead you to numerous blogs which shall guide you. Join online coding platforms like Codechef, Hackerrank, SPOJ for they let you grade yourself relative to the entire world.
During the summer holidays which is very extended, you can give Google Summer of Code a try. You shall learn a lot out of all the research and open-source contributions that you will make in the process. A batchmate, friend and a guy who completed GSoC after his first year, Pawan Dubey has curated a pretty nice answer on how to approach GSoC: How can I prepare for GSoC 2015?
In the course of second year, keep reading, keep coding and keep learning. During the winter break, spend time looking for opportunities where you can Intern for the upcoming summers. See the requirements of the Company/University which have positions for 2nd year interns. Working in a Company/Start-Up shall give you a real insight of how the Corporate Culture is. For some it might even make them realize that they are not meant for desk-jobs. If you are research oriented, try working under a Professor on some active project. The information about Professors and their topics of interests can be obtained by doing a simple search on the University Website. If you want to do a technical internship abroad, there are organizations like IAESTE to your aid. For non technical work there is AIESEC. Also, the summer break is also the time where you can hone your interview skills if in case you want to prepare for the upcoming Campus Interviews (for Microsoft, Amazon, Goldman Sachs), early 5th Semester.
Third year and onward, you can have a look at your resume and decide for yourself what you lack. You shall also learn by looking at your peers and that should be enough to guide you.
I have mostly seen that people lose out due to lack of awareness and not because of lack of ability. So it is very important that you develop the skill of looking out for opportunities as early as you can.
Good luck.
Originally published on Quora.

content:
TLDR; If you are here for just pictures scroll to the bottom.
A little disclosure about me before you start reading this blog, I am Arpan and I hail from India, currently working in Hyderabad. In this post, I am going to endorse a few websites and agencies which helped me to plan for my trip. I am not being paid for advertising any particular firm and these are just my personal choices. I will segregate the blog into timelines relative to the start date of the trip. This blog is not just a travel itinerary helper, I have penned down my experiences and mistakes as well that can be avoided.
April 2018 - 4 months before the trip A couple of my friends and I were itching to do a trip abroad since we had completed the first year of our jobs and it was about time to splurge on a trip. Now as 3 friends sat in a room to decide which location would be the best fit for a week of traveling, Thailand is definitely one of the top choices if you want to travel with a strict budget.
We booked our tickets from Hyderabad to Bangkok (BKK Airport) via Kolkata. Indigo Airlines was the preferred choice and the airline cost was 22000 INR. It included six flights, HYD -> CCU, CCU -> BKK, UTP -> HKT, HKT -> DMK, BKK->CCU, CCU->HYD. We were covering Bangkok, Pattaya and Phuket over a span of 10 days. Undoubtedly, this is a really good price. Overall, this route is pretty convenient. I have met others who travel to Phuket first and then come back to Bangkok. But for a backpacking trip which involves lot of public transport traveling, walking, etc. it is better to be in Phuket in the later half and relax to the fullest. By April we only have the flight tickets and this was going to be our trip planning blue print. Remember that the trip is on, only after the tickets are booked. :) July 2018 - 1 month before the trip A month before the trip is when the planning should gain momentum. You should be looking at hotels, places to visit, modes of traveling, etc. However, my two friends had reasons to not go on this trip. And here I was trying to convince them to not back out. However, this is where the “solo” part of this blog’s caption was seeming to be true. Now I was looking at this trip with a new dimension. Excited yet afraid.
There were some open questions around the arrangement of SIM cards, foreign exchange, VISA etc. I was relying on the on-arrival VISA. Refer to the Thai embassy’s visa on arrival page for the requirements. Quoting from the website, The visit is strictly for tourism purposes.
The passport must be genuine and should be valid for at least 30 days.
You must have a valid address in Thailand whether a hotel or apartment that can be verified.
You must have a confirmed return ticket to show that they are flying out of Thailand within 15 days of entry, as appropriate. Open tickets do not qualify. Traveling overland out of Thailand by train, bus, etc to Cambodia, Laos, Malaysia (including en route to Singapore), Myanmar, etc is not accepted as proof of exiting Thailand.
You may be asked to show your flight ticket on entering Thailand. If you do not possess a flight ticket to show that you will be exiting Thailand within 15 days of entry you will be most likely refused entry.
It will also be necessary to prove that you have funds of at least 10,000 THB per person and 20,000 THB per family during your stay in Thailand.
A fee of 2,000 THB is payable upon entry and is subject to change without notice. It must be paid in cash and Thai currency only.
August 2018 - 1 week before the trip Foreign Exchange - I did some reading as to how to obtain foreign exchange. Remember that in all places of Thailand transactions in THB cash is preferred. That said, most travel agencies and restaurants accept card payment if you are transacting above 500 THB. I used the BookMyForex website to obtain all forms of foreign exchange. It was very convenient and they took about 2 days to provide me with the foreign exchange. I divided the foreign currency into three categories. First category - 50% of my foreign exchange was in THB cash. Second category - 25% of my foreign exchange was in THB Forex Card. Third category - 25% of my foreign exchange was in US Dollar cash. This was primarily to reduce the volume of the cash I was carrying. Hotel Bookings - Since, it was a solo trip and I wanted to limit my budget for hotels I used Airbnb. They have various hotels, home-stays and condominiums to suit your budget. I stayed in about 5 different homes over a span of 10 days. The houses are extremely clean. The hosts are really welcoming and you can learn a lot from them about places to visit, cheaper modes of transport, etc. SIM Card & Travel Insurance - I was not really sure of whether to get the SIM card from India itself or get it in Thailand. Since, I was reaching Bangkok at about 2am, I got the SIM card from CCU Airport. The SIM card was valid for 10 days and costed about 1000 INR. Along with this, I got a travel insurance done for about 1200 INR. So, now I pretty much had everything that would made me confident about the solo trip. Also, having these things ready meant I pretty much had all the pre-requisites required for my on-arrival VISA.
August 9th 2018 - Day of the trip I was aware that there will be a lot of traveling by public transport. Hence, I was carrying just a rucksack. It greatly increased my mobility and hence I would advise everyone to travel as light as possible.
Immigration process in India is pretty straight-forward. Hardly took me 10 minutes to get it done. I got a SIM card and travel insurance from the CCU airport itself. In BKK airport, they will not let you get the baggage unless your immigration is completed. For immigration process at BKK, there are a couple of queues. One of them moves really fast and charges you about 400 THB extra and you will be done in about 45 minutes. The other does not charge you anything extra and usually takes about 2 hours. For everyone who are having a connecting flight to say Phuket/Pattaya, it is advisable to pay the extra 400 THB and get done with this process at the earliest. Bangkok - Day 0 to Day 3 I stayed for 3 days and 2 nights in Bangkok. In this short stay I figured that there are some very generic rules to follow.
Always go by the meter while taking a Taxi. The driver would always quote double the amount. PS - While on road, don’t be amused to see some riders like below. Explore the routes by River Taxi. It costs about 15 THB to go even to the most extreme point. Refer to this guide to Bangkok boats and ferries for a good read about the river taxi system. The river cruise in the evening also gives really nice view of the city which is lit up. I stayed near the Khao San Road for the two nights in Bangkok. Its extremely close to many Buddhist Monasteries like The Great Grand Palace, Wat Arun, etc. Here, you will also get to explore great night life. It felt like a festival but it was hard to believe that every night at Khao San Road is like some celebration. Pattaya - Day 3 to Day 5 Pattaya is a 2-3 hour drive from Bangkok. The cheapest and the best mode to travel is AC bus. “Ekkamai Bus Station” is the place where you can get buses every 1 hour. I reached at about 5 and got an on-spot ticket for 6pm and it costed be about 150 Bahts. I got to know about this through some local friends. It is not listed on any of the blogs that I had read online. Hence, do make a lot of local friends and thrive for such guidance. I was staying at an AirBnb on the Jompien Beach. A walk to the infamous Walking Street was only about 5 minutes. The place served awesome breakfast by the beach side. Now, I do not want to bias travelers but at the same time I cannot resist the urge to write about how much I disliked Walking Street. There was a humongous Indian crowd and it was disgusting to see middle aged men bargaining the rate for solving their mid life crisis. Now, I thought it would be fun to go to a strip club. But, the dancers were not really dancers. Most of them looked drugged and it was sad to see the amount of emphasis on sex. “Boom Boom” as they call it. I went to “The Sanctuary of Truth” which is an hour drive from Jompien Beach. It would be preferable to visit here during lunch as it has a beautiful lake sort of thing and you can enjoy lunch there. I was lucky to see a 30 minute cultural show that they had organized for the visitors. Never had I thought that I would enjoy something so traditional. Amongst the other places that I visited in Pattaya were “The Alcazar Show” and “The Big Buddha”. There is also an aquarium and a painting museum which you can see if you free for an evening. Phuket - Day 5 to Day 9 Phuket was the last leg of this trip. By now, I had been traveling relentlessly without a break and was starting to get a bit tired. Phuket was also the place for which I had no reservations or plans apart from my stay at a condominium.
Unlike Bangkok and Pattaya, I was not staying at a jam-packed locality in Phuket. My stay was a good 30 minutes travel from Patong Beach which is kind of the most touristy place in Phuket. My host was kind enough to rent me a brand new scooter which made traveling super easy. In software engineering, we have something called as a SOP which is the sequence of procedures that we apply for doing something. Phuket has certain SOPs in terms of the places to travel. There are abundant travel agencies each providing similar sight seeing, island tours and trips. I headed to one of these travel agencies and booked 3 island tours which were going to keep me occupied for the next 3 days. The first day was the Coral Island and Raya Beach, second was James Bond Island and the third was Phi Phi Island. On day 1, I headed to Coral Islands and Raya Beach. As expected the water was clear and the sand was white. We stoped at a bay for snorkeling. Being a non-swimmer, I could still enjoy viewing the marine life underneath. We headed to an extremely beautiful wood house by the sea for lunch. The speed boat experience was full of adventure as well. In one of the pictures below you can see how transparent the water is. And yes, in the water the the green objects are fishes and not leaves. On day 2, we headed to James Bond Island. This day we traveled by a cruise which was slow and not as much fun as a speed boat. Nevertheless we did canoeing. You can even request your guide to let you canoe by yourself. Though it is not as easy as it looks. On day 3, we headed to Phi Phi Island. I was also about to see Maya Bay which for me was going to be the highlight of the trip. Again, we were on a speed boat. Because of the weather being overcast, the sea was extremely rough. This was by far the most adventurous thing that I have done. I felt the trip was life threatening was kept wondering how that small boat kept floating in the rough sea. A lot of travelers quit the trip mid way and were sent back to shore on a bigger, more stable boat. We again did canoeing at Maya Bay and say some other islands like the Monkey island. Overall, this day was my last and undoubtedly the best during the trip. There is a famous tourist attraction called as “The Big Buddha” in Phuket. I really wanted to go here but due to the island tours being tiring, I always used to head back home and rest. On the final day, my phone ran out of battery and I couldn’t navigate home. I spent almost 2 hours going around Phuket. Now, it was around 8PM and I could spot some well lit structure on a hill top. As I draw closer, I realized it was the statue of Buddha. I am not really a believer of fate but as fate would have it, I got to see “The Big Buddha”. Most of the evenings in Phuket, I used to go around Patong beach. There is the famous “Bangla Road” which is a must visit in Phuket. It is very similar to the Khao San Road in Bangkok. There are numerous restaurants around Patong Beach where I used to relax in the evenings. Common Myths - Busted No insects as edibles. Yes, but I found baby scorpions at Khao San Road. Unlike in India, there are no dogs and cows on streets. Thailand could possibly be where Tom and Jerry live. There are just cats and mice all over the place. In the last 10 days, I travelled 3 cities and 12 islands. I went on a flight, train, bus, bike, boat, ship and cruise. I went to places with ticket. I went to places ticket less. I did things that in hindsight seems risky. I was lucky to have not fallen ill. I was lucky that rains did not play a spoilsport. I was lucky to have met people who wanted me to enjoy this trip as much as I wanted to. Credits to Amit Pandey and Kartik Parmar for ditching me on this trip. Had it not been for them, the solo trip would never have been possible. Lastly, thank you the people of Thailand. I’d hope the people of India become half as much receptive to foreigners as you have been.
Originally published on Quora.

content:
I had applied for internship at Microsoft (SWE Intern ‘16) and Amazon (SDE Intern ‘17).
This resume is from when I was in 5th Semester. Microsoft had been on campus for Interns. I basically had nothing at that time to construct a good looking resume apart from my test scores and a few competitions. The biggest takeaway is that the interviewers did not question me anything on my resume since there was nothing fancy. I was strictly judged on the basis of a few programming questions. I was not very confident of a few small projects that I had done. And I decided to exlude them from the resume. In my opinion, anything that you are not confident about should not make it to your resume. I applied to Amazon off campus. I was in my 7th Semester and by now had a few things to fill my resume. By now, there were a lot of things to be put in the resume. I had to pick the ones which were the best indicators of my abilities. I had moved to using a Latex formatter instead of a free online resume creator. Overall, resumes should evolve depending on where you are applying to. Ensure that it’s a single page and precise because the recruiter will probably have less than a minute to glance at your resume. Be absolutely honest with what you put in your resume. You would be tempted to include things for the sake of it. However, it is worth resisting this temptation.

summary:
I had applied for internship at Microsoft (SWE Intern ‘16) and Amazon (SDE Intern ‘17).

  • This resume is from when I was in 5th Semester. Microsoft had been on campus for Interns.
  • I basically had nothing at that time to construct a good looking resume apart from my test scores and a few competitions.
  • The biggest takeaway is that the interviewers did not question me anything on my resume since there was nothing fancy. I was strictly judged on the basis of a few programming questions.
  • I was not very confident of a few small projects that I had done. And I decided to exlude them from the resume. In my opinion, anything that you are not confident about should not make it to your resume.
title: Authoring a good Resume

content:
I interned at Amazon Development Centre (Hyderabad) for 5 months at the start of 2017 while I was in my 8th Semester. In my 7th Semester, I had been trying hard to secure an internship in some startup or corporate. Amazon was in my wish-list because I had friends who had interned there during the summers and had awesome things to say about the experience. During December 2016, I was contacted by a recruiter for an intern position after a senior had referred me for an Intern position. After a couple of rounds of interview, I got selected for a position in Amazon’s Hyderabad campus. I was really happy because Hyderabad was a city I was familiar with and I had a few friends interning there. After doing a little bit research about my team, I got to know I would be working with the Amazon Home Services team. Back then I never knew Amazon was into such a business line for selling services to customers and I thought it to be pretty interesting.
Fast-forward to the start of the internship, Amazon had arranged for our travel and had given us a 15 day stay at a 5-star hotel. I had a lot of friends who were also interns and were staying in the same place, hence this was one hell of a fun ride. Every day we would wake up early, enjoy the sumptuous breakfast buffet. This is where I met a lot of other co-interns who also were interning with Amazon Home Services (AHS). And I also met others interning from all sorts of teams like Amazon Payments, Amazon Transportation, Amazon Fulfilment, etc.
On day 1, there was a briefing for all the interns about the Amazon Culture in general. Amazon takes a lot of pride in their culture and hence these sessions spanned for the entire day. People were invited to share their experiences and it was wonderful to see how people grew from being Interns to Principal Engineers at Amazon. We were given a small diary which is pretty symbolic and has the infamous quote “It’s Still Day 1” which is Amazon’s philosophy to always continue having the same enthusiasm throughout the journey as if it’s the first day. There were also the mention of the famous Amazon Leadership Principles which continues to be the keys for succeeding at Amazon.
We were then given instructions to collect our laptops and other accessories. Most interns got a new MacBook. I then went to the designated area to meet my team and manager. At this point my senior manager mentioned that the team had gone on a weekend trip to Goa and decided to extend their stay. In my mind, I was thinking that what an awesome group of people they must be to have such trips. At the same time feeling unlucky about missing the trip by a small margin. Nevertheless, the MacBook kept me busy for the rest of the evening.
The next day I met all of my team members and was introduced to my manager and mentor. My manager (who I still work with) was just about 6 years elder to me and had been an intern at Amazon. In fact it was fun to know that most of my team members had been ex-Interns at Amazon before starting out as full timers. Overall, it was a pretty young team with the eldest member being about 8 years older than me.
Since I was to intern for about 5 months, my manager and mentor had worked out a plan for a bunch of tasks that I will do based on my progress. My first task was a commit that got deployed to Amazon’s Retail Website. At the time I felt a bit shocked that the team trusted me with coding something that was to be deployed onto the production website as my first task.
However I was quick to realise that over here there was no real difference between an intern and a full-timer. There was no difference between a new member and a tenured member. As an individual you are responsible for certain things and people expect you to be in terms with it.
Amongst all the perks, Amazon was generous enough to provide interns with the same amount of facilities as a full time employee for boosting productivity. With just a button click you can get the hardware you need. And there are multiple self service vending machines for other peripherals like mouse/keyboard/headphones. I experimented with multiple sets of monitors to see what suits me. The two monitors arrangement continues to be my favourite till date and I still use this arrangement.
Overall I was happy with my first task and felt good about completing the same. I also got introduced to the strict code reviews and testing procedures that are kept in place to ensure faulty code does not leak into production. Days passed by and I kept reading more and more internal documentation and go about doing my tasks. As I got closer to my team-mates, we would go out for ad-hoc fun sessions like Go-Karting, Dinners, X-Box matches, Poker sessions and streaming cricket matches. This really helped to break the ice with some of the senior members of the team who intimidated me because of their sheer knowledge and experience.
Coming back to my internship, Amazon Home Services had 5 interns including me. All of us belonged to different colleges and were part of different sister teams. We would regularly meet to discuss how it’s going for each other and often poke fun around not being able to understand a lot of internal documentation and processes. We went on a trip to watch an IPL match with the entire organisation. Below is a picture of that day with the fellow interns Ashutosh, Nirmal, Manya Setia and Arushi Garg who continue to be good friends of mine.
Overall the first 3 months of my internship was pretty easy-going and was the ramp up phase where we just got used to all the processes for deploying code into production. I also got a lot of free time to work on a couple of side projects that I was pursuing from college. By the end of 3 months, I was already given my main project which required me to independently do some designing, all the implementation and rolling out to production. As the end of my internship approached, my work hours increased. I still cherish this phase because at times the entire office would be empty and only the interns would be there working on their tasks. I would plug in my head phones and just loved this phase because of the sheer amount of code I was writing and deploying to production. Back then deploying code to production gave me an adrenaline rush. Below is a picture of me in the last week of my internship writing those unit tests for covering each branch. One of the interns sneaked in to capture this picture and I am lucky to still have it. We still have a good laugh about these times.
In the last couple of weeks my manager and mentor also explained to me the conversion process from Intern to full time. The process was pretty simple. It required each intern to document in a template all the tasks they have worked on and the milestones they have met. Post an initial evaluation and feedback from peers, the manager discusses with a Bar Raiser on the conversion decision. And post that a hiring decision is made. Sometimes a few candidates are required to do additional 1 or 2 round of interviews. I completed all my documentation and completed the exit formalities. Usually all interns are told about their hiring outcome by the last date, however in my case it was delayed and I was told to wait a while due to some last minute crunch.
My teammates organised a wonderful farewell. Over the past 5 months there was a personal connect that each of us had developed. Since the Amazon Home Services organisation was a 45 member team back then, the feeling was that of a start-up within the massive Amazon Corporate. The farewell tradition comprised of a speech by the outgoing interns and questions asked by our peers to embarrass the shit out of us. I met a bunch of super smart folks with whom I connected with not just from work perspective but also from a personal point. I was not sure if I would convert and join back as a full timer. Hence, with a pinch of uncertainty I ended my internship.
I ended the internship on a Friday. On Saturday I returned back to my home-town. On Monday morning when I woke up (first working day post I left), I had an email from the recruiter conveying that they were extending a full time offer to me. I was really happy and more than that I had a lot of respect for the team, the recruiter and the company for getting back to me with the result so swiftly. I breathed a sigh of relief and that marked the end of my Amazon Internship.

title: My Amazon Internship Experience!

content:
I interned at Microsoft IDC (Hyderabad) which is their second biggest campus in the world outside of Redmond in the summers of 2016. Hence, I am literally reliving the experience after 4 years as I write this answer. A little bit on how I got the offer in the first place, Microsoft visited our campus in August 2015 to hire SDEs and SDE Interns and that’s when I was able to clear about 4 rounds of interviews. I got a cool T-Shirt with the Microsoft logo which I still treasure. I had about a year’s gap from the time I received the offer until I actually started interning in May 2016. There was a huge build up and me and my friends were brimming with excitement thinking about the opportunity that lies ahead of us. Microsoft does a really nice job of ensuring that Interns do not have to think anything apart from the Internship itself. They took care of our stay for a two month period and provided us with transportation which made our 30 minute daily commute super smooth. They arranged for our daily meals within the campus and our round trip flights from the city where we interned at. Apart from this there was a good stipend which made me realise my renumeration value for the first time.
Fast forward to Day 1 of internship, we entered the majestic IDC campus which was truly no less than a wonder. I personally felt it looked better during night-time.
There were multiple buildings within the campus and we were guided to our designated building and conference rooms. The recruiter had invited a few of the Software Engineers (including a few of our Alumni) to ease the nerves and tell us about what we can expect from the internship. From then on, we were set free to explore every nook and corner of the campus. I met my team, my mentor and my manager. Took some time to setup my work-desk setting up the software and hardware.
It was the best feeling to have unlimited Azure Credits, enterprise licensed software for Visual Studio and Windows 10 and for the first time developing software on Windows Platform felt seamless (as against Pop-Culture) and what most of us were used to while working on Linux.
Now we all were on a mission to explore the many perks within our building. And no post about the MS IDC campus can be complete without the mention of the infamous pantry. There was unlimited stock of almost all refreshments by Amul, Coke, Green Tea, Coffee, Cookies, CCD. You name it and it was there.
There were multiple playing facilities like Cricket, Football, Gym facilities, Table Tennis and Pool. Sukul Bagai and I had a very religious routine of our TT breaks and Pool sessions. And by the end of the internship we were pretty good at these sports.
Gradually all of us got really engrossed with work. Everyday we would have to read about a lot of techniques and patterns to be able to make progress. The office culture was pretty open and people around were really approachable and helpful. People were serious about their work during the day time and by the evenings everything toned down. Initially I was a bit hesitant to do anything apart from work at my work-desk but then my team-mates joined me for streaming a couple of tennis matches. All of us were Roger Federer fans.
This part becomes important to understand that here it’s not about just work. There is a very nice balance between work and play over here. And hence it really helps if you maintain this balance in your life before joining a corporate.
There were social nights organised for all Interns. These sessions was also an opportunity for everyone to socialise with students from so many other colleges. It was nice to know how things worked in other institutes and their aspirations.
Hence, a very important part of your internship would be meeting other people and getting to know them. All of them excelled in programming, open-source, competitive coding, etc. and were amongst the best in the country.
There was also a very nice event organised within the campus. Kanan Gill and The Local Train were invited to perform and all of us had a gala time. I along with a couple of friends Shubheksha Jalan and Mahathi Gunturu were lucky to click a picture with the band members of The Local Train. That’s us with Raman Negi and other members of the band.
Microsoft also does a lot of internal hackathons. I participated in a couple of them. For the first one, I read some internal documentation for the newly released Microsoft Bot Framework. And wrote some code for a chat bot to automate a few tasks for my team. My team really appreciated the effort to complete this since it was not a milestone from my internship perspective. The second hackathon was an internal Data Science Challenge organised by the Bing Division in which all of the interns, employees including data scientists were allowed to participate. I along with a couple of my friends Sukul Bagai and Rohit Malhotra registered for this competition as we had a common penchant towards ML problems. It was a two day challenge with a prediction related problem statement around the Customer’s Ad Click Rate Prediction (Click-Through Rate Prediction on Kaggle). For the first day we were too lazy and none of us even bothered to ping each other to start participating in the challenge. Also we had been thinking what chance did we even have when there were so many seasoned employees and data scientists participating in the challenge. On the second day, we really gave it a thought since we could see some of the fellow intern teams doing well on the leader board. Sensing that we had a chance, we quickly got together, arranged three bean bags with a lot of refreshments and started breaking down the problem. We debated and eliminated approaches and started testing our model with actual customer data-sets. After spending about one full day we were continuously ranking in the Top 5 of the challenge. By now we were surely motivated to be Top 1. We made our final submission and were fairly confident of being in the Top 10 at the least. Our models would be assessed on hidden data-sets and we were to receive the results on the following day. We received the results the next day and to our surprise our model had the best accuracy. We received some cash prizes and some recognition from the leaders and were ecstatic.
The reason why I shared this story along with the above screenshot is to signify the journey from deciding to not even participate in the challenge to actually winning it. This was for sure one of our better achievements in our internships.
Hence the important learning here was that the best opportunities would not be given to you. You will need to look for them and grab them. We were not even close to being the best in ML and a lot of times you don’t have to be the best. Teamwork, enthusiasm and zeal to complete a task goes a long way.
In the final week of our internship, we all were sad and anxious about our project demos. There were also some interviews scheduled (1 or 2) depending on our performance in internship. And based on this a decision was made to make an offer or not. I was super happy to receive an offer and it was the first offer made to me for a full-time job. I went around the campus one last time, clicking some cliched photographs with the Microsoft logo and my lanyard. I am lucky to somehow have a backup of these photographs and being able to share this with all of you through this answer.
That’s it folks! That was the end of a super productive summers.
